create.name: Jean Houston
create.bio:
Jean Houston (1937–2026) was an American writer and teacher who spent nearly seventy years asking what ordinary people are capable of becoming. Born in New York City, the daughter of a comedy writer, she studied at Barnard College. In the 1960s she and her husband, Robert Masters, took part in officially approved research into LSD; once that work was banned they turned to imagery, movement and imagination as drug-free routes to fuller awareness, and ran the Foundation for Mind Research together. The anthropologist Margaret Mead was a close friend and lived with the couple for some years.

From 1983 she led the Mystery School, weekend gatherings held twice a year that mixed talks on myth, history and science with dance, song and guided exercises. Her books, among them The Possible Human, The Search for the Beloved, A Mythic Life and Jump Time, invite readers to see their own lives as part of a larger story. She trained community leaders for United Nations development programmes in an approach she called Social Artistry, served as chancellor of Meridian University, and in later years wrote the Future Humans trilogy with Anneloes Smitsman. She died in Ashland, Oregon, on 16 May 2026, aged 89.

books.title: The Possible Human: A Course in Enhancing Your Physical, Mental, and Creative Abilities
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: Her best-known workbook: a sequence of exercises in movement, sensing, imagery and memory meant to wake up abilities most people leave unused. Readers work through it alone or in a group, a few practices at a time.

books.title: The Search for the Beloved: Journeys in Mythology and Sacred Psychology
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: Houston's account of what she called sacred psychology, drawn from her Mystery School years. Old myths and stories become guided rituals through which readers look for a deeper relationship with the sacred in their own lives.

books.title: Jump Time: Shaping Your Future in a World of Radical Change
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: Written at the turn of the millennium, this book argues that humanity is living through an unusually fast period of change and asks how individuals and societies might grow into it rather than resist it.

books.title: A Mythic Life: Learning to Live Our Greater Story
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: Part memoir, part teaching: Houston tells her own story, from a chaotic childhood to work with leaders around the world, and uses it to show readers how to find the larger pattern in their own lives.

books.title: A Passion for the Possible: A Guide to Realizing Your True Potential
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: A short, practical introduction to her approach, with exercises for widening the senses, thinking in new ways and connecting with a sense of purpose.

books.title: Life Force: The Psycho-Historical Recovery of the Self
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: A study of how the human sense of self has changed across the ages, paired with exercises that let readers revisit each stage in their own experience.

books.title: The Wizard of Us: Transformational Lessons from Oz
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: Houston reads the Oz story as an American myth of growth, following Dorothy and her companions as guides to finding a mind, a heart and courage, with practices along the way.

books.title: The Hero and the Goddess: The Odyssey as Mystery and Initiation
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: Homer's Odyssey retold as a year-long initiation, with each episode turned into reflections and group exercises for modern readers.

books.title: Godseed: The Journey of Christ
books.author: Jean Houston
books.description: A reading of the life of Jesus as a pattern of inner transformation that anyone may walk, framed as a series of guided experiences.

books.title: The Quest of Rose: The Cosmic Keys of Our Future Becoming
books.author: Anneloes Smitsman, Jean Houston
books.description: The first book of the Future Humans trilogy, written with Anneloes Smitsman: an allegory that follows a young woman's journey to explore new science, indigenous wisdom and the next steps in human development.

courses.title: Unlock Your Quantum Powers
courses.description: A seven-week online course led by Jean Houston and still offered by Evolving Wisdom. It works with a handful of capacities she called quantum powers, such as a looser sense of time and steady creative energy, through weekly sessions and exercises.

courses.title: Awakening to Your Life's Purpose
courses.description: Jean Houston's seven-week online course, still offered by Evolving Wisdom, on recognising a personal calling and shaping work and relationships around it, with reflection and practical exercises.

free_resources.title: Jean Houston interview: full transcript (Buddha at the Gas Pump)
free_resources.description: The complete written transcript of her long 2018 conversation with Rick Archer, free to read. It covers her childhood, her research into human capacities and her view of the times we live in.

sprint.tier_evidence: Ascended Master (died 16 May 2026); owner's decision, 4 Nov 2026
flags: Archive rule: no-estate figure (maximum curation discipline). The Jean Houston Foundation's site (jeanhoustonfoundation.org, read 4 Nov 2026) is a single 2021 splash image with a contact address and nothing else, and her own site jeanhouston.com is frozen (2012 pages, a 2020 Covid letter, a parked Kajabi link), so no foundation or family visibly runs the work. Evolving Wisdom still sells two of her recorded courses, but it is a commercial distributor, not an estate, and no institution carries her teaching on (she was chancellor of Meridian University, but its site was not used as a legacy home).

NO PHOTO: image_urls is empty. No free Commons image of her exists (Wikidata Q6170855 has no image; a Commons search found only a crowd shot at a Living Enrichment Center event, not of her). Wikipedia's infobox photo (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jean_Houston.jpg) is a non-free fair-use upload, not usable. Her own site's photos sit under /images/, which jeanhouston.com's robots.txt disallows, so they were not fetched. The Foundation's only image is a logo/text splash with other people's faces. Owner to decide on a photo (e.g. permission from Meridian University or her publishers).

website_url is her own Meet Jean page (https://www.jeanhouston.com/Jean-Houston/): still online but unmaintained since about 2012 (home page shows a 2020 letter); the Foundation's site is only a splash page, so neither is truly maintained. booking_url left null.

Death and dates: born 10 May 1937, died 16 May 2026 in Ashland, Oregon, aged 89, per Wikipedia (citing The New York Times, 18 June 2026) and Wikidata; New Dimensions' tribute (17 June 2026) and the Future Humans channel's video description give the same years.

Offerings: the two Evolving Wisdom courses link to Infusionsoft order forms, the only course links on evolvingwisdom.com (home page read 4 Nov 2026; nothing copied); the order forms were not opened, so price is 'Contact for pricing'. Evolving Wisdom's home page still describes live weekly sessions and group coaching, which cannot now include her; owner may prefer to leave them out.
Left out the third Evolving Wisdom programme, The Influencer's Masterclass (with Claire Zammit): business and leadership training for coaches.

Videos are all on the hosts' official channels (BatGap, Science and Nonduality, OWN, Thinking Allowed, The Chopra Well, Dr Sue Morter, Unity Community of Ashland, Future Humans, Home for Humanity); no re-uploads or AI voice clones used. All 11 passed oEmbed (200) on 4 Nov 2026. She has no channel of her own; Future Humans is co-run with Anneloes Smitsman, so it is not set as youtube_url.
Video 'Jean Houston's Early Spiritual Awakening' (OWN, SuperSoul Sunday) is 2 min 45 s, just over the 2-minute floor; kept because it is the official clip.

Books: ISBNs confirmed on Open Library (/isbn/<isbn>.json → 200, right title, author Jean Houston OL217855A): https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0874778727.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0874778719.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1591810183.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0062502824.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0062515314.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0835606872.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1582703795.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0345365674.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0835606775.json, https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1990093116.json. ISBN-10s are as found in Wikipedia's list or converted from booksellers' ISBN-13s; Amazon never opened, so the ASIN is the ISBN-10 and may be an older edition.

The Quest of Rose (1990093116): Open Library lists only Anneloes Smitsman as author; Houston's co-authorship comes from the publisher listing and the Future Humans and Chopra Well videos. Smitsman is not on Spiritpedia, so author is plain text.
Bio says she served as chancellor of Meridian University: from the Home for Humanity video description and web search results, not from Meridian's own site (not opened).
Free resource is BatGap's full transcript page of the 2018 interview (also listed as a video); only one free resource found that is clearly free and genuine.
Dry-run note: 'Life Force' shares its title with Tony Robbins' 2022 book already on Spiritpedia (id 178); hers is a different book (Quest Books, 1993, ISBN 0835606872), so both stay.

Offering images set to null: the Evolving Wisdom order forms carry no image and Evolving Wisdom's images may not be copied. (The ingest dry-run itself requested the two order-form URLs with its own honest user agent when looking for images.)
left_out: The Varieties of Psychedelic Experience (with Robert Masters, Open Library 0892818972): genuine and well known, but a guide to LSD effects; left out under no-estate curation, owner may add.
The Passion of Isis and Osiris (0345424778), Mystical Dogs (1930722133) and Manual for the Peacemaker (0835607097): confirmed on Open Library but over the 10-book limit.
Mind Games and Listening to the Body (with Robert Masters): older titles; the second is health-framed.
The Wizard of Us ISBN 1582703744 and A Passion for the Possible 0062504827 were wrong guesses (Open Library returned other books); replaced by 1582703795 and 0062515314.
Interview with Dr. Jean Houston by Rev. Kathy Zavada (RpLllq4oelI): its description talks about how we self-heal; borderline health framing, left out.
The New Story with Lynne McTaggart (Future Humans): McTaggart is the main speaker.
Dr. Jean Houston & Dr. Anneloes Smitsman The Lure of the Future Human (EvolutionaryLeaders): 146 views, a near duplicate of the Future Humans talks.
The Quickening - Dr Jean Houston (EARTHwise Centre): 4-minute excerpt, low value.
New Dimensions' four archived Jean Houston programmes ($1.99 MP3 each): sold by a radio archive, not an estate or Evolving Wisdom.
jeanhouston.com programmes (Mystery School weekends, mentoring, 2012 event calendar): long past and no longer offered.
Facebook and X links on her site: facebook.com is blocked to us and the X account could not be opened, so not linked.
